newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway shares hit life peak, but seen falling.
newsitem.headline: Norway shares hit life peak, but seen falling.

text.p: The Norwegian Stock Exchange charged to another record close on Tuesday but some dealers said they believed the index would not rise much further now.
The Total share index ended at 1,178.74 points, up 0.49 percent from Monday's record close of 1,173.01 points.
Turnover was relatively thin at 800 million crowns.
Industrial giant Norsk Hydro was the most traded share at 112 million crowns and closed 0.27 percent up at 365 crowns.
"Norsk Hydro, Kvaerner, Norske Skog and Elkem have performed well recently, but I doubt the market will continue much higher than this. I think we will see profit-taking," one dealer said.
"Buying is more selective now. Blue chips are not doing so well any more. Players are picking shares. There will be focus on small caps soon," he said.
But Bergesen, Norway's largest shipping company, looked strong, its A share rising 1.48 percent to 171.50 crowns.

Ocean Rig, which jumped 8.02 percent on Monday on reports that an oil company was close to signing a rig deal with the group, was the second most traded share at 47 million crowns. The share initially continued to rise on Tuesday on a report it had sealed contracts with Statoil and Saga Petroleum. An official denial sent the share down and it closed unchanged.
